### A-2 Model fitting details {.unnumbered}

The fishery selectivity likelihood has multiple modes, so the reported
Rceattle configuration used data-based fishery-selectivity starting values and two fitting
stages. The first stage disabled the annual selectivity deviations to establish
the selectivity and abundance scale. The second stage restored the deviations
and used the first-stage solution as its initial values. This sequence produced
a small maximum gradient and `OK` status. With the direct ATS/AVO
coefficient-increment penalty, the Hessian condition number was approximately
489,000; its weakest direction remained in the shared ATS/AVO annual
selectivity deviations (`sel_coff_dev`) rather than fishery/CPUE.

The complete fitting sequence, including the empirical starting values and
the two estimation stages, is in the
[two-stage fitting script](<2024 EBS pollock.R>) and is run with
`Rscript "2024 EBS pollock.R"`. The nine-peel implementation is in the
[retrospective script](<2024 EBS pollock two-stage retrospectives.R>) and is
run with `Rscript "2024 EBS pollock two-stage retrospectives.R"`.

The retrospective peels repeat this sequence after recalculating the data-based
selectivity starting values for each terminal year. Because `sel_coff_dev`
contains annual random-walk increments at age, each peel fixes the terminal-year
fishery and mirrored catch-per-unit-effort increments at zero. This holds their
terminal selectivity-at-age curves at the preceding-year curves.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-initial-developments
#| tbl-cap: "Disposition of the Rceattle development components."

initial_development_status |>
  gt() |>
  cols_width(
    Item ~ px(35),
    Initial_development ~ px(120),
    September_review_result ~ px(170),
    Plan_Team_interpretation ~ px(190)
  ) |>
  cols_label(
    Initial_development = "Development component",
    September_review_result = "Review result",
    Plan_Team_interpretation = "Interpretation"
  ) |>
  tab_style(
    style = cell_text(weight = "bold"),
    locations = cells_body(columns = Item)
  )
```

### A-3 Jitter and natural-mortality profile {.unnumbered}

The [extended-diagnostics runner](R/run_rceattle_5_8_1_extended_diagnostics.R)
generates both the 50 jitter fits and the age-3-and-older natural-mortality
profile with `Rscript R/run_rceattle_5_8_1_extended_diagnostics.R`.

The 50 phased jitter runs test sensitivity to dispersed starting values.
Forty-eight returned to the best objective within numerical precision. Two
received `WARN` status and reached an inferior mode with an objective increase
of approximately
`r sprintf("%.1f", max(jitter_summary$Delta_objective, na.rm = TRUE))`.
This reproduces the pre-existing multimodality and shows why convergence of one
run is not sufficient evidence that the global mode was found.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-jitter-summary
#| tbl-cap: "Rceattle 5.8.1 phased-jitter results for the fitted configuration. Delta objective is measured from the best of 50 runs."

jitter_summary |>
  group_by(Convergence_status) |>
  summarise(
    Runs = n(),
    Minimum_delta_objective = min(Delta_objective),
    Maximum_delta_objective = max(Delta_objective),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  gt() |>
  fmt_number(
    columns = c(Minimum_delta_objective, Maximum_delta_objective),
    decimals = 3
  ) |>
  cols_label(
    Convergence_status = "Status",
    Minimum_delta_objective = "Minimum delta objective",
    Maximum_delta_objective = "Maximum delta objective"
  )
```

The age-3-and-older natural-mortality profile was evaluated from 0.15 to 0.50.
The grid minimum occurred at
`r sprintf("%.2f", mortality_profile[["Age-3+ natural mortality"]][which.min(mortality_profile$Objective)])`,
but the objective changed by only
`r sprintf("%.2f", max(mortality_profile$Delta_objective))`
across the entire grid. The profile is therefore shallow and does not support
precise estimation of natural mortality from these data alone.

```{r}
#| label: fig-natural-mortality-profile
#| fig-cap: "Profile of age-3-and-older natural mortality for the Rceattle 5.8.1 configuration. Points are evaluated grid values and the vertical axis is objective difference from the grid minimum."
#| fig-alt: "A shallow natural-mortality profile has its grid minimum near 0.20; the objective difference rises to about 3.82 at 0.50."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4.5

ggplot(
  mortality_profile,
  aes(x = `Age-3+ natural mortality`, y = Delta_objective)
) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "gray55", linetype = 2) +
  geom_line(color = "#1b9e77", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(color = "#1b9e77", size = 2) +
  labs(x = "Age-3+ natural mortality", y = "Delta objective") +
  ggthemes::theme_few()
```

### A-4 Composition-likelihood sensitivity {.unnumbered}

The [5.8.1 summary script](R/finalize_rceattle_5_8_1_analysis.R) fits the
standard-multinomial sensitivity and writes the summaries used here when run
with `Rscript R/finalize_rceattle_5_8_1_analysis.R`.

The Rceattle configuration uses the supported `MultinomialAFSC` composition
likelihood with a robustness constant of 0.001 added to observed and expected
proportions. A standard multinomial fit without this constant was retained as
an observation-model sensitivity. Both fits reached small gradients and
received `OK` status. The final configuration's residual least-identified
direction remained in the shared ATS/AVO annual selectivity deviations.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-composition-likelihoods
#| tbl-cap: "Composition-likelihood sensitivity for the Rceattle 5.8.1 configuration. Raw objectives are shown for run provenance but are not compared because likelihood constants and conventions differ."

model_summary |>
  filter(!grepl("2D AR1", Model)) |>
  mutate(
    Model = case_when(
      grepl("standard multinomial", Model, ignore.case = TRUE) ~
        "Standard multinomial",
      TRUE ~ "Final configuration"
    ),
    Composition_likelihood = recode(
      Composition_likelihood,
      MultinomialAFSC = "AFSC multinomial",
      Multinomial = "Standard multinomial"
    )
  ) |>
  select(
    Model,
    Composition_likelihood,
    Objective,
    Maximum_gradient,
    Convergence_status
  ) |>
  gt() |>
  fmt_number(columns = Objective, decimals = 3) |>
  fmt_scientific(columns = Maximum_gradient, decimals = 2) |>
  cols_label(
    Composition_likelihood = "Composition likelihood",
    Maximum_gradient = "Maximum gradient",
    Convergence_status = "Fit status"
  ) |>
  cols_width(
    Model ~ px(115),
    Composition_likelihood ~ px(130),
    Objective ~ px(85),
    Maximum_gradient ~ px(85),
    Convergence_status ~ px(60)
  )
```

Relative to the `MultinomialAFSC` configuration, the standard
multinomial sensitivity changed spawning biomass by
`r sprintf("%.2f", comparison_summary$Mean_absolute_percent[comparison_summary$Method == "Standard multinomial sensitivity" & comparison_summary$Quantity == "Spawning biomass"])`%,
recruitment by
`r sprintf("%.2f", comparison_summary$Mean_absolute_percent[comparison_summary$Method == "Standard multinomial sensitivity" & comparison_summary$Quantity == "Recruitment"])`%,
and total biomass by
`r sprintf("%.2f", comparison_summary$Mean_absolute_percent[comparison_summary$Method == "Standard multinomial sensitivity" & comparison_summary$Quantity == "Total biomass"])`%
on average in absolute percentage terms.

### A-5 2D age-by-year AR1 selectivity sensitivity {.unnumbered}

The penalized-effects initialization and subsequent Laplace fit are in the
[two-stage fitting script](<2024 EBS pollock.R>) and are run with
`Rscript "2024 EBS pollock.R"`. A separate
[fixed-scale follow-up](<2024 EBS pollock 2D AR1 fixed sd test.R>) can be run
with `Rscript "2024 EBS pollock 2D AR1 fixed sd test.R"`; it is a development
check and is not the sensitivity summarized below.

The 2D AR1 sensitivity applied an age-by-year field to the shared fishery and
catch-per-unit-effort selectivity block over 1964--2024. The age-year deviations
were first fit as penalized effects to initialize the field and then integrated
as random effects with a Laplace approximation. The initialized Laplace fit
failed the gradient, Hessian, and bound checks.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-ar1-selectivity-parameter-summary
#| tbl-cap: "Diagnostic 2D AR1 fishery-selectivity correlation and scale estimates."

ar1_selectivity_parameter_summary |>
  select(-Final_internal_value) |>
  gt() |>
  fmt_number(
    columns = c(
      Penalized_effects_initialization,
      Final_random_effects_fit
    ),
    decimals = 3
  ) |>
  cols_label(
    Quantity = "Quantity",
    Internal_parameter = "Rceattle parameter",
    Penalized_effects_initialization = "Penalized effects",
    Final_random_effects_fit = "Random-effects fit"
  ) |>
  tab_source_note(
    source_note = paste(
      "Correlations are on the -1 to 1 scale; the deviation scale is a",
      "positive standard deviation. The fit failed convergence checks."
    )
  )
```

The failed random-effects fit had a maximum marginal gradient of 19.7 on
`rec_pars`, a non-invertible Hessian, 61 `log_F` parameters at their configured
bounds, and `FAIL` convergence status. These estimates remain diagnostic.

```{r}
#| label: fig-development-selectivity-ridges
#| fig-cap: "Development comparison of relative fishery selectivity for ADMB, the Rceattle configuration, and the failed 2D age-by-year AR1 sensitivity."
#| fig-alt: "Three side-by-side ridge plots compare relative fishery selectivity by age and year for ADMB, the Rceattle configuration, and the failed 2D age-by-year AR1 sensitivity."
#| fig-width: 15
#| fig-height: 10
#| out-width: "100%"

ggplot(
  selectivity_ridges,
  aes(
    x = Age,
    y = Year_factor,
    height = Relative_selectivity,
    fill = Model
  )
) +
  ggridges::geom_ridgeline(
    scale = 3.8,
    alpha = 0.28,
    color = "black",
    linewidth = 0.2,
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  facet_wrap(vars(Model), nrow = 1) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(
    "ADMB reference" = "#1f78b4",
    "Rceattle NonParametricPM" = "#1b9e77",
    "Rceattle 2D AR1 (failed)" = "#d95f02"
  )) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(1, 15), breaks = 1:15) +
  labs(x = "Age", y = "Year") +
  ggthemes::theme_few() +
  theme(
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
    panel.spacing.x = grid::unit(1.2, "lines")
  )
```

### A-6 Acronyms {.unnumbered}

This appendix follows the glossary convention in the [Alaska Stock Assessment
Report (`asar`) package](https://github.com/nmfs-ost/asar)
[@schiano2026asar]. The project glossary uses ASAR's `\newacronym` format and
adds terms specific to this Rceattle comparison. The quoted label "PM" is a
model name.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-acronyms
#| tbl-cap: "Acronyms used in this working paper."

project_glossary |>
  select(Acronym, Definition) |>
  gt::gt() |>
  gt::cols_width(
    Acronym ~ gt::px(105),
    Definition ~ gt::pct(75)
  )
```
